1. Beginner Astronomy Corner
A section for students who are curious about astronomy but do not know where to begin. Not everyone starts with equations, telescopes, or technical knowledge. Some people only know planets and constellations at first, and that is completely okay. This section could have simple guides, basic skywatching tips, astronomy vocabulary, and “start here” resources.

2. National Event Calendar
A shared calendar where different ISAAC chapters can post upcoming stargazing sessions, workshops, talks, competitions, webinars, and collaborative events. This would help chapters stay connected and also allow students from different universities to participate in each other’s activities.

3. Interactive Chapter Map / Chapter Showcase
A map or showcase of all ISAAC chapters across India, with their club pages, social links, ongoing activities, and major projects. This would make the national network feel more alive and help younger chapters learn from older or more active ones.

column2: NISER Astronomy Club (National Institute of Science Education and Research)
column3:
NISER Astronomy Club (NAC) is a student-run club based at NISER, Bhubaneswar. The club aims to create and motivate the interest of students towards the wonders of the sky. We engage in a diverse set of activities including telescope observation sessions, astrophotography tutorials, instrumentation and observations, outreach programs. We have our own annual magazine Kshitij which offers once-in-a-year opportunities to students all over the country to work with our talented team of editors and publish articles. The heart of the club lies in the imaginative dream of many of the club's former leaders - KALPANA, our ROR observatory housing the club's 11-inch Schmidt-Cassegrain and 8-inch Newtonian telescopes. The soul of the club on the other hand, lies in each and every member of the club and their relentless passion for stalking the night sky.

email: astroclub@niser.ac.in
instagram: astroclub_niser
youtube: @niser_astronomy_club
website: https://astroclub-niser.github.io/

Other than the usual list of activities mentioned above, our club in December 2025, organized an astrocoding workshop in collaboration with Naxatra, IISER Berhampur's Astronomy club. We also were awarded the 2nd prize in the Astronomy-themed experiments competition, 2024, organized by the Astronomy Center for Educators(ACE) of IUCAA, Pune, for the experiment that determined the orbital period of the Galilean moons using a smartphone and a 6" telescope for data acquisition. One of the astrophotographs taken by our club was highly commended in Astronomad's APERTURE: Indian Astrophotography Competition, 2024. In the same year, the photograph was exhibited at M.P. Birla Planetaium, Kolkata. Our club also celebrated the first anniversary of KALPANA on last year's National Space Day, 23rd August. We have also had talks by numerous faculties from around the world.

column4:
Here at KMC Physics Astronomy Club, we aspire to build a research aptitude for all those who love the cosmos and aspire to build a career in Astrophysics and Astronomy, and adjoining fields. So, over the past year we have been working on several student led formal research projects. 
Besides, we run a monthly social media newsletter, on our instagram and linkedin pages that happens to cover the latest works and news in the fields of Astronomy, Astrophysics and Space Technology. 

As of now, we are working on three independent student led research projects, what follows is a small description of each of these projects

Project Ocean Worlds examines the habitability of Europa and Titan by studying agnostic biosignatures. The study contrasts Europa’s saline environments with Titan’s hydrocarbon lakes using computational simulations to predict mission findings.

21 cm Signal Project Hydrogen is the universe's most abundant element, forming stars and galaxies. Its hyperfine spin-flip transition reveals a galaxy's rotational velocity, hydrogen density, and self-absorption. This project focuses on building an affordable horn antenna radio telescope at 1420.4 MHz (21 cm line) to map the Milky Way's hydrogen density and rotation.

JWST Early Galaxy Conundrum Project aims to study theoretical and computational models that work on explaining the missing keys in the Lambda CDM model found by JWST data sets like JADES. The work aims to study the models that explain the formation and evolution of galaxies at high redshifts and at the edge of the Universe that are too massive for size. 

We have a separate group associated with a fixed plan and timeline assigned for each of these projects.
Besides this, we also have a few short term instrumentation and experimental works lined up for the upcoming tenure, and also a new research project that is currently in its ideation phase. 

At ISAAC, we would be grateful to be able to share our works in accordance with these projects ,our newsletter, and our upcoming research projects.
column5:
From our perspective, apart from individual club pages and blogs, we would like the ISAAC homepage to have features that help visitors connect with the astronomy community, discover opportunities, and learn something new every time they visit.

First, we would like to see a National Event Calendar that brings together upcoming astronomy-related events, workshops, webinars, observation sessions, competitions, and outreach programs organized by different ISAAC chapters. Having all events in one place would make it easier for students and astronomy enthusiasts to stay informed and participate actively.

Second, an Interactive India Chapter Map would be very useful. It would allow users to explore ISAAC chapters across the country, learn about their activities, and find contact information. We believe this would strengthen collaboration between chapters and help newcomers find a local astronomy community to join.

Third, we would like a Resource Library containing astronomy articles, observation guides, recorded lectures, beginner tutorials, and recommended learning materials. Such a section would make the website valuable not only as a community platform but also as a learning resource for students at different levels.
column6:
For our KMC Physics Astronomy Club, I think, few things are required which, if hosted by ISAAC website will be a great help. The first would be a research paper guide to different research problems/fields. Surely, there are many introductory astronomy or astrophysics book that provides good guide to any field. Yet, reading research paper is an essential thing for anyone's research journey, thus, if the website host research paper guide to different topics like Radio Astronomy, Galaxy formation, AGN, etc.

Second, since our club is doing different independent research projects which involves computational aspect very much, providing codes and guides for simulations or data analysis will be of great help too. Also, if ISAAC hosts about the ongoing research projects across all the clubs in it, it will be a quite enriching opportunities for every club to look into the research being done by there fellow mates.

Additionally, as many undergrad students often stuck in looking for internships or research groups working on problems of their interest. Thus, if the website host such related datas or references, that would not just help our club but every undergrad student in general.

column2: Space Technology Students' Society, IIT Kharagpur
column3:
We are the Space Technology Student’s Society (better known as spAts), the official student body under Kalpana Chawla Space Technology Cell, which is the contact point of ISRO and IIT Kharagpur. spAts was founded when a diverse group of students sharing a common interest in space science and astronomy came together. It has since been the motto of spAts to spread awareness among the masses about the cosmos and simultaneously enhance our knowledge and understanding of space through activities and fun. Each individual of our Society has a thirst for knowledge and love being engaged in learning. Some lean towards the best technical stuff, some are interested towards the theoretical side of things, some love astronomy, reading, discussing current events and some love capturing the beauty of the night sky. We learn about stuff by building projects, having loads of discussions, exploring new skills and of course - dedicating towards space.

Our primary contact points are: Email - spats.iitkgp@gmail.com
Instagram - https://www.instagram.com/spats.nssc.iitkgp
LinkedIn -  https://www.linkedin.com/company/spats
Facebook - https://www.facebook.com/spAts.iitkgp

We annually conduct National Students' Space Challenge (NSSC), a national level Astro-Tech Fest, dedicated exclusively to space science, astronomy, and space technology, bringing together students who share a deep interest in the exploration and advancement of the space domain. We recently started a great initiative of writing and publishing Literature Reviews on various space-related domains and as of now we have published  20+ Literature reviews which can be accessed via our website (https://www.spats.co.in/publication). Using our 8" newtonian reflector telescope, we have gathered various astrophotographs and combined them into an Astro Photography Catalogue (again can be accessed from https://www.spats.co.in/publication). Our work is not only limited to IIT Kharagpur students. We conduct Space Technology Awareness Camp (STAC) for students outside of the KGP campus, which provides them an unparalleled opportunity to launch into space, through hands-on activities like water rocketry workshops, space quizzes and astro-presentations.
